newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares close higher, boosted by Astra.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares close higher, boosted by Astra.

text.p: 1500 GMT - Swedish shares closed higher on Thursday ahead of the long midsummer weekend, injected by strong gains from drugs company Astra amid market rumours of imminent FDA approval for its asthma treatment Pulmicort in the U.S.. * Stockholm general index rises 0.85 pct to 2,914.77 * Turnover a fairly hefty 6.74 billion crowns * Astra rose 7.0 crowns to 137. * Telecoms major Ericsson dropped 7.5 crowns to 289.5. Brokers partly attributed the weakness to a PaineWebber report that ranked the stock as 'unattractive'. * Appliance maker Electrolux rises 17 to 565 crowns.
Swedish shares closed higher on Thursday ahead of the long midsummer weekend, injected by strong gains from drugs company Astra.

Astra rose seven crowns to 137 amid market rumours of imminent approval from U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for its asthma treatment Pulmicort Turbuhaler in the U.S.. The company said it had no news from the FDA.
The Stockholm general index climbed 0.85 percent to 2,914.77 in fairly hefty turnover of 6.74 billion crowns.
"It's been a good pace today and it is very much Astra that has driven up the rest of the bourse," said one broker.
"But there could also be a bit of the half year earnings effect in this and so we could see this good pace continuing next week."
The market started the day weaker, depressed by telecoms major Ericsson that ended 7.5 crowns lower at 289.5 crowns.
Brokers partly attributed the weakness to a PaineWebber report that ranked the stock as 'unattractive' and lowered earnings per share forecasts for 1997 and 1998.
Appliance maker Electrolux rose 17 to 565 crowns as the market continued to react to news of a radical restructuring.
Speciality tool maker Sandvik rose 0.5 to 209 crowns. It announced it had bought U.S. twist drill maker Precision Twist Drill Co for an undisclosed sum.
The forestry sector index rose 2.31 percent, the second biggest mover after the drug index that rose 4.53 percent.
Enskilda said it was positive on Scandinavian forestry stocks and had Stora and AssiDoman among its favourite Sweden companies.
"Our valuation model indicates the forestry sector has an upward momentum potential of 25 percent," Enskilda said.
